chapter.v:
Sing this
funeral song for the princes of Israel

with these
words: “What was your mother? She was a lioness among the lions! She lay down in her place among the young lions and reared her cubs.

She raised
one of her cubs, and he grew up to be a young lion. Once he had learned how to tear up his prey, he started eating people.

But when
the nations heard about him, he was caught in their trap. They used hooks to drag him away to Egypt.

When she
realized that the hope she had been waiting for was gone, she made another of her cubs into a young lion.

He went
around with the other lions, and became strong. Once he had learned how to tear up his prey, he started eating people.

He tore
down their fortresses and destroyed their towns. All the people living in the country were appalled when they heard him roaring.

Then the
people of the countries all around attacked him. They threw their net over him; he was caught in their trap.

They used
hooks to put him in a cage and took him to the king of Babylon. They led him away and imprisoned him so his roar wasn't heard any more in Israel's mountains.

Your mother
was like a vine planted in your vineyard at the waterside. It produced a lot of fruit and had many branches because it had plenty of water.

Its branches
were strong like rulers' scepters. It grew high above the tree canopy. People could see how tall and full of leaves it was.

But it
was uprooted in anger and thrown down on the ground. The east wind blew and dried up its fruit. Its strong branches were stripped of leaves and they withered. Then they were burned up in the fire.

Now the
vine has been replanted in the desert, in a dry and waterless land.

A fire
blazed out from its main trunk and burned up its fruit. None of its branches that were once like a ruler's scepter are strong any more.” This is a funeral song and is to be used for mourning.
